questions.question_text: If $|A| = 18$, $|B| = 24$, and $|A \cap B| = 7$, what is $|A \cup B|$?

options.why: Adds $|A|$ and $|B|$ directly without subtracting the overlap $|A \cap B|$.
Adds the overlap instead of subtracting it: $18 + 24 + 7$.
Subtracts the overlap twice from the sum of the sets.

questions.question_text: In a cohort of students, $|A| = 32$, $|B| = 29$, and $|A \cup B| = 48$. What is $|A \cap B|$?

options.why: Adds $|A| + |B|$ without subtracting the union $|A \cup B|$.
Subtracts $|A|$ from $|A \cup B|$ instead of using the inclusion-exclusion formula.
Subtracts $|B|$ from $|A \cup B|$ instead of finding the intersection.

questions.question_text: Two sets satisfy $|A \cup B| = 55$, $|B| = 31$, and $|A \cap B| = 12$. What is $|A|$?

options.why: Subtracts $|B|$ from $|A \cup B|$ without adding the intersection back.
Confuses the size of set $A$ with the overlap $|A \cap B|$.
Adds the intersection to the union instead of rearranging the addition rule.

questions.question_text: Sets $P$ and $Q$ are disjoint ($P \cap Q = \varnothing$). If $|P| = 21$ and $|Q| = 34$, what is $|P \cup Q|$?

options.why: Subtracts the set sizes $|Q| - |P|$ instead of adding them.
Confuses the union of disjoint sets with their empty intersection.
Multiplies the sizes of the two sets instead of adding them.

questions.question_text: In a surveyed group, $45$ people belong to set $M$ and $16$ belong to both $M$ and $N$. How many people belong to $M$ but NOT to $N$ ($|M \cap N'|$)?

options.why: Adds the overlap to the set total instead of subtracting it.
States the overlap count rather than the count of elements in $M$ only.
States the total count of set $M$ without removing the elements in $N$.

questions.question_text: A universal set has $|\xi| = 80$ items. Subsets $A$ and $B$ satisfy $|A| = 42$, $|B| = 35$, and $|A \cap B| = 14$. How many items belong to neither set ($|(A \cup B)'|$)?

options.why: Calculates $|A \cup B|$ instead of the count outside the union.
Calculates $80 - (42 + 35)$ without accounting for the double-counted intersection.
Subtracts $|A|$ from $|\xi|$ and ignores set $B$ entirely.

questions.question_text: In a class of $50$ students, $30$ participate in coding club, $25$ participate in robotics club, and $8$ do neither. How many students participate in BOTH clubs?

options.why: Calculates $30 + 25 - 50$ without excluding the $8$ students who do neither.
Adds the $8$ non-participants to the total instead of subtracting them from the universe.
Finds the number of students who do robotics only rather than both clubs.

questions.solution_text:
Students in at least one club:
$50 - 8 = 42$
$|C \cap R| = |C| + |R| - |C \cup R|$
$= 30 + 25 - 42$
$= 13$

questions.question_text: Two sets satisfy $|A| = 2k + 5$, $|B| = 3k + 2$, and their overlap is $|A \cap B| = k$. If the union has $|A \cup B| = 51$, what is the number of elements in the intersection $|A \cap B|$?

options.why: Finds the size of set $A$ ($2(11) + 5$) instead of the intersection.
Finds the size of set $B$ ($3(11) + 2$) instead of the intersection.
Solves $(2k + 5) + (3k + 2) = 51$ without subtracting the overlap $k$.
